items.d: If the deal goes through, it would be the latest in a long string of giant compute deals Anthropic has struck over the past year.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 4:39 PM PDT · October 19, 2026 Image Credits: Kyle Grillot/Bloomberg / Getty Images Lucas Ropek Nscale and Anthropic are reportedly in talks for yet another $45B compute deal A little over a month ago, Anthropic and AI infrastructure provider Nscale announced a $45 billion compute deal . Now the duo may be about to do it again. Bloomberg reports that the two companies are said to be on the verge of announcing yet another $45 billion compute deal, citing people familiar with the matter. Those sources cautioned that talks are still underway and that the details could change. If the deal goes through, it would be the latest in a long string of giant compute deals Anthropic has struck over the past year . TechCrunch reached out to Nscale and Anthropic for more information and will update this story if we hear back. The massive amount of money being sunk into AI compute deals has spooked a certain segment of investors , who worry that companies are spending too much money for too little profit. Still, Anthropic has pressed on with such partnerships, driven by the belief that it will all pay off in the end. Both Anthropic and Nscale are also currently pursuing IPOs. Anthropic is still expected to go public this year. Nscale is also seeking to go public, although Bloomberg reported on Monday that the company is experiencing investor pushback over its proposed valuation of $30 billion. items.t: Microsoft says AI agents are like insider threats as ‘frontier models can’t be trusted’
items.d: Microsoft wants enterprises to closely watch the agents that employees use with systems not controlled by AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic.
items.fullText: Microsoft on Monday introduced new security features designed to protect enterprises from the growing threat of AI agents. The launch comes as Microsoft continues to warn enterprises about the dangers of AI and agents. Perhaps the most notable addition is Guardian Agents , a new feature intended to monitor the AI agents a company uses. Guardian Agents is part of Project Perception, a product introduced in June. Project Perception was Microsoft’s answer to powerful hacking models like Anthropic’s Mythos and Fable and OpenAI’s security vulnerability scanning system Daybreak. Project Perception originally launched three classes of agents: a “red team” that acted like hackers and attacked, a “blue team” that detected the red team and assessed the vulnerabilities they found, and a “green team” tasked with fixing them. The product was designed around the assumption that AI hackers would come from outside the company. But lately, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has been warning that the AI enemy may be the very agents enterprises have deployed and are paying for, much like a rogue human employee, otherwise known as an “insider threat.” Earlier this month, in his private blog , Nadella warned that it’s time to stop trusting AI model providers, even if they offer assurances of safety and security with their agentic products. He wants enterprises to implement separate systems, not controlled by the AI labs, to watch and control the agents that those AI labs’ products launch. “We are deploying these complex agentic systems and models, with access to our most sensitive data and giving them the ability to take mission-critical actions on our behalf!” he wrote. “We simply can’t outsource responsibility for what intelligence does on our behalf. items.t: Hackers hit AI coding tool OpenCode, running up charges on users’ AI accounts
items.d: OpenCode is an open source AI coding agent that's become a popular alternative to Claude Code and Cursor. But hackers got into part of its online platform and stole some users’ API keys, and the AI tools it turned to for help kept refusing to look at the malicious code.
items.fullText: OpenCode , an open source AI coding agent that has been gaining ground among developers as an alternative to Claude Code and Cursor, said Saturday that attackers broke into an older system overnight, affecting 1.4% of users of its online platform, OpenCode Console, where some users store the API keys, or digital passwords, they use to access AI services. As the OpenCode team struggled to keep pace with the attack, the scramble to respond highlighted a growing problem: Companies without vetted access to AI models with fewer safety restrictions have a hard time defending against large-scale, AI-driven cyberattacks. “We had a security breach last night related to a large-scale distillation attack that impacted 1.4% of OpenCode Console users,” the company wrote on X. “We have notified them all this morning via email.” Users who did not receive an email were not impacted, the company said. While the company didn’t specify how the distillation attack occurred, leaked API keys can help users in countries with restricted access to American models generate the high volume of outputs needed for that process. Some skeptics called the framing an overstretch, arguing that the incident was a straightforward breach whose use for distillation remains unproven. Overnight, developers began posting spending alerts and unauthorized charges on Reddit and X: “I saw my Open AI, Anthropic, and Google AI spend alerts all fire off before going to bed wondering what was going on,” a developer wrote . Other users reported charges in the hundreds of dollars on individual accounts; a few described totals above $1,000. Anthropic and Google both blocked the API keys they believed were exposed, while OpenAI said it worked with OpenCode to restore access and refund its API customers for credits used in the attack. items.t: Elon Musk and Anthropic make promises to give the public a piece of the AI pie
items.d: Elon Musk and officials at AI giant Anthropic are pledging to give coveted shares in their companies to the general public as concerns about AI’s economic and societal impact continue to pile up.
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Elon Musk and Anthropic make promises to give the public a piece of the AI pie The promises come as the public has broadly soured on AI and concerns about its economic impact grow. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Elon Musk is awarded the National Medal of Science during the Golden Age of American Innovation Summit in Washington on Oct. 8. Kent Nishimura / AFP via Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 19, 2026, 10:39 AM EDT By Rob Wile Elon Musk and officials at AI giant Anthropic are pledging to give coveted shares in their companies to the general public as concerns about AI’s economic and societal impact continue to pile up . “Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America,” Musk posted on X on Monday. “This will be the first of many.” One SpaceX share is currently valued at about $150. With approximately 72 million children under the age of 18 in the U.S., Musk’s donation would currently be worth about $10.8 billion — less than 2% of his current net worth. He provided no additional information. Musk could not be reached for additional comment. His statement comes one day after officials at Anthropic said the company would commit 5% of company shares to a “public benefit fund” in order to address “labor market impacts” of AI. In a statement, Anthropic officials said the fund could make charitable donations or direct money to “specific populations,” emphasizing the fund’s “versatility.” “Given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed,” they said. Anthropic has been preparing for an initial public offering — releasing its stock for trading on public markets — that analysts say would value the company at more than $1 trillion. The company has long championed employees’ charitable giving by promising to match their donations. Dario Amodei, co-founder and chief executive officer of Anthropic. NVIDIA today released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, an open 120-billion-parameter model that delivers the fastest task completion and highest accuracy for specialized always-on agents. Joining it are two new edge models: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, optimized to balance intelligence and speed per GB for local agentic workloads, and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB, optimized for intelligence per GB for fast conversational agents. Super VL and Bolt 74B-A9B are available now, with Bolt E4B coming Oct. 23. The three open models together cover the full range of agent deployments, from large enterprise servers down to edge devices and local hardware. Any organization that wants to run agents on NVIDIA infrastructure now has an open, optimized model for their tier, without having to choose between capability and deployability. Super VL and Bolt join the Nemotron family alongside Lightning and Ultra. Lightning, released in August, handles high-throughput workloads; Ultra handles the hardest reasoning tasks; and Bolt brings intelligence to the edge. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL: Frontier Accuracy at One-Fifth the Size Super VL, built in collaboration with the Nemotron Coalition , delivers leading accuracy on multimodal agentic tasks — instruction following, tool use, multistep business workflows, and visual understanding — comparable with NVIDIA’s largest reasoning model at roughly one-fifth the parameter count. items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Eight states sue OpenAI over ChatGPT’s alleged harms to users Kansas Attorney General Kris Kobach said states “are not going to hold our breath” for federal legislation to keep AI companies in check. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Eight states sue OpenAI claiming ChatGPT harms children 01:17 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 14, 2026, 7:18 PM EDT By Angela Yang and Joe Kottke Eight states sued OpenAI on Wednesday, accusing it of deceiving parents about the safety of ChatGPT. The coordinated lawsuits — filed individually in Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, West Virginia, Arkansas, Arizona, Idaho and Montana — target the AI giant for the harms its generative AI chatbot is alleged to have caused to ​children in those states. “OpenAI, they wanted to be the first to market. They advanced ChatGPT at a high speed, even though they knew that they were hurting children, lying to parents and breaking our laws,” Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird said at a news conference announcing the legal action. “Everyone must follow the law.” The company’s flagship AI model, ChatGPT, launched the generative AI boom in November 2023, when it exploded into mainstream culture, and quickly became the biggest chatbot in the world. This summer, it surpassed 1 billion global monthly active app users . In recent years, users have increasingly turned to it and other chatbots for everything from friendship to therapy, as well as a slew of agentic tasks in their personal and professional lives. Bird was joined at Wednesday’s news conference by Kansas Attorney General Kris Kobach, Nebraska Attorney General Mike Hilgers and West Virginia Attorney General JB McCuskey. items.fullText: European Cities Deploy NVIDIA-Powered AI Agents to Run Smarter Urban Operations Across the region, local software, infrastructure and integration partners are using NVIDIA accelerated computing and models to build agentic applications that improve city operations and public services. October 13, 2026 by Charbel Aoun 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Keeping a city running means making decisions that affect residents every day — from when to repair a road to how to use energy more efficiently. Across the EMEA region, cities and local software, infrastructure and integration partners are using NVIDIA accelerated computing to build physical AI agents and digital twins that help teams make those decisions. These applications can anticipate maintenance needs, guide urban planning and make public services more responsive. Software partners including ABA Technology , Akila , Galene AI , Honeywell Technologies , K2K , Linker Vision , Milestone , Onetera , ThinkDeep and Younite AI are using NVIDIA physical and agentic AI to develop solutions for city operations and public services. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/linker-vision.mp4 Video courtesy of Linker Vision and MVRDV. NVIDIA Cosmos open models and the NVIDIA Metropolis Blueprint for video search and summarization (VSS) help agents interpret video and identify conditions, such as traffic congestion, equipment condition, underused spaces and safety hazards, that need attention. NVIDIA Nemotron open models enable developers to build agents that reason over information, respond in natural language and deploy digital twins with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries. Projects span Belgium, Finland, France, Italy, the Netherlands, Poland, Sweden, the U.K. and elsewhere.
